ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Specific Financial Information Act; Act No. 15620, as amended), Enforcement Decree of the Specific Financial Information Act; Act on Regulation and Punishment of Concealment of Criminal Proceeds (Proceeds of Crime Act; Act No. 15648); Commercial Act (Act No. 14248), including trade name, Yuhan Hoesa formation and registered office requirements; Customs Act (Act No. 18413) on bonded warehouse operators in free trade zones; and the Financial Services Commission Regulation on Beneficial Owner Identification for Financial Transactions and AML/CFT internal controls.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certificate of Company Registration)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Korean District Court Registry Office for the registered head office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Path A (Hague Apostille Convention state): official court registry certificate is presented directly to the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) Apostille Section for a single Hague Apostille; no consular step. Path B (non-member state): official court registry certificate is authenticated by MOFA and then presented to the relevant Korean Embassy/Consulate for consular legalization. Path A and Path B are mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Registered Facts and Corporate Existence)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Korean District Court Registry Office, with supplementary tax clearance certificate from the National Tax Service (NTS)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Path A: certificate issued by the district court registry is legalized through a single MOFA Hague Apostille; NTS tax clearance is attached as a certified public document. Path B: for non-Apostille states, the registry certificate is authenticated by MOFA and then consular-legalized at the Korean Embassy/Consulate. No sequential combination of Apostille and consular legalization is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney Appointing Incorporation Agent and Local Representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporators, initial shareholders and directors of the intended Korean Yuhan Hoesa, notarized by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Path A: notarize the board resolution and power of attorney before a Korean notary public, then obtain a Hague Apostille from MOFA; consular legalization is not used. Path B: notarize, obtain MOFA authentication, then obtain consular legalization at the Korean bilateral mission of the relevant non-Apostille state. The two authentication routes are alternative, never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Charter of the Yuhan Hoesa)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporators and initial shareholders, certified by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Path A: certified Korean Articles of Association are translated into English as needed, notarized, and submitted to MOFA for Hague Apostille. Path B: certified and notarized Articles are authenticated by MOFA and then submitted to the Korean consular post for consular legalization. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive channels and may not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter Confirming Professional Banking Relationship and Source of Funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Korean commercial bank or recognized foreign correspondent bank maintaining the proposed UBO and corporate relationship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Path A: bank reference letter is signed by an authorized bank officer, notarized by a Korean notary public, and apostilled by MOFA. Path B: notarized bank letter is authenticated by MOFA and then consular-legalized for non-Apostille states. Apostille and consular legalization branches are parallel and exclusive; they never operate in the same documentation chain.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport, Certificate of Identity and Proof of Residential Address of Ultimate Beneficial Owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or consular post in the country of residence of each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Path A: identity documents are notarized in the country of origin and apostilled by the competent authority of that Hague Apostille Convention state; no Korean consular action is added. Path B: identity documents are notarized and consular-legalized through the Korean Embassy/Consulate having jurisdiction over the non-Apostille issuing state. Path A and Path B remain mutually exclusive.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory AML/CFT screening must cover (i) domestic and foreign politically exposed persons as defined by the Specific Financial Information Act and FATF Recommendation 12, including PEP family members and close associates; (ii) OFAC SDN, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions, EU consolidated sanctions, and Korean government-designated sanctions published by KoFIU and Korea Customs Service; (iii) adverse media, negative news, regulatory warnings, Interpol notices, and domestic court/regulatory enforcement records; (iv) escalated Enhanced Due Diligence, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation, personal data confirmation, and independent verification by outside counsel. The screening protocol must run before onboarding, at every Swift Wire or local clearing event, and upon any change in beneficial ownership; electronic screening audit trails must be retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IROS), official online company registration and trade-name search portal (www.iros.go.kr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Korean Commercial Act, a company trade name must be in Hangul; foreign-origin names must be transliterated phonetically into Hangul and registered. The registered name must contain a clear corporate type indicator for Yuhan Hoesa. The four-tier naming standard requires: (1) corporate type indicator, (2) distinctive Hangul trade name, (3) phonetic Hangul transliteration of any foreign name, and (4) Romanized alias for international banking. The registered trade name may not be identical or deceptively similar to a pre-registered name of another Korean entity in the same business scope.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry rejects the proposed trade name, the applicant must receive a written refusal citing the specific statutory ground. The applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the rejecting District Court Registry and the Court Administration Office within 14 days of service; the appeal must set out the legal basis, corrected name tokens, consent from any conflicting nameholder, or evidence of acquired distinctiveness. The registry must issue a written disposition. If the administrative appeal is unsuccessful, the incorporators may file an application for revocation or cancellation with the Administrative District Court under the Administrative Litigation Act within 90 days from service of the final refusal. A new name cannot be substituted into an appeal; any amended name must start a fresh clearance cycle through IROS, pay the revised search fee, and obtain a new clearance record within the 30-day validity window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office, commercial mailbox, or shared drop-box address is rejected by Korean tax authorities, courts, banks, and the Korea Customs Service for this bonded warehouse industry. The Commercial Act requires a registered head office that is physically ascertainable; the National Tax Service requires a substantive business location for VAT and corporate tax registration; Korean banks require a physical presence, identifiable signage, and an in-person signatory meeting before opening corporate accounts. For a Free Trade Zone bonded depot, the Korea Customs Service additionally demands a physical warehouse facility, customs supervision access, inventory control systems, lockable bonded storage, and an on-site operational team. Limited shared-office space within the Free Trade Zone may be tolerated if it contains a dedicated lockable unit, business signboard, records room, and staffing, but a standalone virtual mailbox is legally insufficient.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated quantified risk is 85% probability of an unannounced physical inspection by municipal tax authority or Korea Customs Service within the first 12 months of bonded depot licensing. Mandatory checklist for on-site verification: (i) bonded warehouse boundary and approved location, (ii) secure physical storage and inventory segregation, (iii) electronic inventory and accounting records, (iv) CCTV and restricted-access logs, (v) payroll and employment records showing local staff, (vi) original lease contract and rent receipts, (vii) corporate seal and signing authority, (viii) daily inbound/outbound bonded cargo records, and (ix) risk-rated UBO documentation. Any failure in the checklist will trigger customs license suspension, tax penalty, or criminal referral.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Chapter 5, Limited Liability Company (Yuhan Hoesa) Articles 543 through 568; Commercial Registration Rules; Foreign Investment Promotion Act Articles 2, 5, 6 and 28; Customs Act Articles 178 through 192; Act on Designation and Management of Free Trade Zones Articles 4, 9, and 14.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court of the Republic of Korea having territorial jurisdiction over the company's registered office, accessible through the Supreme Court of Korea electronic registration system (iROS).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation and application for registration of incorporation (commercial registration) of a Yuhan Hoesa under the Korean Commercial Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital is imposed on a Yuhan Hoesa under Korean law. The articles of incorporation must state the subscribed contributions, and every member must fully pay the subscribed amount before the incorporation registration. Capital may be as low as KRW 10,000; there is no mandatory escrow or blocked account, but the deposit must be evidenced by a bank certificate from the Korean bank and, if applicable, a foreign investment remittance certificate issued under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic filing portal: HomeTax (hometax.go.kr). Customs-excise processing for the Free Trade Zone is administered by the Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS (unipass.customs.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity establishing a Yuhan Hoesa LLC with a domestic fixed place of business (including a bonded warehouse depot in a Free Trade Zone) must file a business registration application under the Business Registration Act and the Value-Added Tax Act with the district head tax office that has jurisdiction over the principal or branch place of business. The application is submitted through HomeTax and must attach the certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, evidence of the physical business address (lease or ownership proof), the FTZ operator license, and, where no domestic office has yet been opened, an appointment of a tax representative. The NTS examines the application, performs an on-site or documentary verification of the place of business, and issues the Business Registration Certificate containing the 10-digit Business Registration Number, which concurrently functions as the VAT identification number. Foreign entities that do not have a Korean place of business but are required to file VAT for digital services or import-related transactions must appoint a Korean tax representative and register separately with the NTS for VAT purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Yuhan Hoesa is a domestic corporation under the Korean Commercial Act; subject to Korean corporate income tax on worldwide income, 10% VAT obligations, local income tax surtax, and no pass-through classification)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean tax law does not provide a check-the-box election comparable to the United States. A Yuhan Hoesa LLC is automatically taxed as a domestic corporation; partnership-style pass-through, branch-equivalent classification, or hybrid entity election is not available. Separate consolidated corporate tax is available only to a qualifying domestic parent-subsidiary group and is not a tax classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 0 for a corporation; business registration is mandatory from commencement. Simplified taxable treatment (KRW 80,000,000 annual turnover threshold) is available only to individual sole proprietors, not to Yuhan Hoesa LLC. In the Free Trade Zone, import VAT and customs duties are suspended on goods entering the bonded depot until the goods are released into the domestic market; the depot operator must nevertheless be VAT registered for all domestic taxable sales and supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic e-Tax Invoice issuance is mandatory under the Value-Added Tax Act for all VAT invoiceable supplies. Yuhan Hoesa must issue electronic tax invoices through the NTS HomeTax e-Tax Invoice system, and the e-invoice data are transmitted to the NTS no later than the day after issuance. For final-consumer retail transactions, the cash receipt system must be used where required. The Korean system does not impose a pre-clearance fiscal-stamp or government-authorization API; anti-fraud control is embedded in the mandatory digital certificate, real-time reporting, invoice sequence monitoring, and matching of e-invoice data with customs and foreign-exchange declaration data.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported from Korea, including further exports out of a bonded warehouse or Free Trade Zone after deposit, are zero-rated under the Value-Added Tax Act where the exporter holds the export declaration, the goods leave Korea through a customs-approved method, and the sale consideration is receivable in foreign currency. Qualifying cross-border services, international transport, and services directly connected with exported goods may also qualify for zero rating where supplied to nonresidents or performed with statutory evidence. In the bonded depot context, the 0% rate is substantiated at the time of actual export from Korea; earlier movement into the bonded area only suspends customs and VAT, and supplies released into the domestic market are subject to import VAT and customs duties.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Declaration Certificate issued by the Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS
Bill of Lading (sea freight) or Air Waybill (air freight) evidencing departure of the goods from Korea
Foreign Exchange Receipt Certificate issued by a Korean Foreign Exchange Bank evidencing actual receipt of export proceeds (equivalent to an Inward Remittance Certificate)
Commercial Invoice and detailed Packing List
Bonded warehouse release or departure record from the Free Trade Zone management system
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service cross-check e-Tax invoices, export declarations, bonded warehouse inventory records, and foreign-exchange receipts. If export zero-rating is not substantiated or the foreign-currency proceeds are not received within the required 180-day repatriation period, the zero rate is reversed, the 10% VAT on the supply is assessed retroactively, and additional tax (unpaid-tax additional tax and negligent or fraudulent reporting additional taxes) is imposed under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Value-Added Tax Act. Where invoices are false or fraudulently zero-rated, criminal sanctions apply under the Tax Evasion Punishment Act, and the taxpayer may be barred from the expedited exporter VAT refund program.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) acting jointly with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the foreign exchange administration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Customs Act of South Korea
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a largely liberalized current account regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, meaning trade-related payments for goods, services, and current transfers are freely convertible through licensed foreign exchange banks. However, capital account transactions are subject to a notification, post-reporting, or prior approval framework administered by the Ministry of Economy and Finance and delegated to domestic banks. For a Yuhan Hoesa operating a bonded warehouse in a free trade zone, inbound equity capital from non-resident shareholders must be routed through a foreign currency deposit account at a domestic foreign exchange bank, supported by a Foreign Investment Notification under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act if the investment qualifies as FDI. Dividend and profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are generally permitted once corporate governance and tax clearance documentation, including audited financial statements, shareholder meeting minutes, withholding tax filings, and a certificate of tax payment, are submitted to the bank. Although no mandatory surrender of export proceeds to the central bank is currently imposed, all export-related foreign currency receipts must be collected within statutory deadlines and deposited or settled through a domestic foreign exchange bank. The Korean won is not freely tradable outside the regulated onshore and offshore FX markets for unlicensed non-bank entities, but authorized banks may execute KRW/USD and other major currency transactions for underlying trade and FDI liquidity. The overall convertibility risk is moderate, with strict documentation, transaction purpose verification, and intra-group transfer pricing scrutiny for trade-related flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Enforcement Decree, export proceeds must be collected within 6 months from the date of export declaration unless an extension is granted by the foreign exchange bank. Extension beyond 18 months, up to 36 months, may be permitted for large-scale capital goods or deferred payment export transactions with supporting contracts. There is no mandatory conversion ratio to Korean won; all export proceeds must be repatriated into a domestic foreign currency deposit account at a licensed foreign exchange bank. The exporter must submit a Foreign Exchange Payment Receipt Certificate and related customs declarations to the bank to evidence timely receipt. Failure to repatriate within the statutory timeline triggers a reporting obligation to the Ministry of Economy and Finance and potential administrative penalties.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech EMIs and digital-only banks are not viable as primary settlement institutions for this Yuhan Hoesa bonded warehouse mandate. Under the Banking Act and the Electronic Financial Transactions Act of South Korea, only domestic commercial banks or licensed foreign bank branches can operate resident Korean won corporate accounts, perform foreign exchange services, and interface with the Korea Customs Service electronic payment and bonded depot systems. Offshore digital EMIs are not authorised to hold KRW liquidity in the Hong Kong or Singapore clearing infrastructure for Korean customs duty payments, cannot issue compliant MT103 settlements into the Korean domestic clearing network, and are legally barred from servicing corporate treasury needs such as documentary LCs and import duty payments. The maximum permissible role for a fintech EMI is ancillary corporation payment facilitation through a duly licensed partner bank, but the Yuhan Hoesa must maintain its primary accounts, FX hedging lines, and customs payment rails at a domestic Tier-1 commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Statutory directors and authorized signatories must appear physically in a domestic branch in South Korea for corporate account onboarding. Remote opening is not permitted for a medium-risk enhanced bonded warehouse entity with non-resident ownership. If a non-resident statutory director cannot travel, the bank may accept a limited, notarized and apostilled power of attorney appointing a resident officer or resident legal representative to appear in-branch. During the physical visit, the bank will conduct a face-to-face interview with the ultimate beneficial owner or appointed representative, verify passports, and review corporate formation documents. The final account activation is contingent on successful completion of a compliance committee review and approval by the bank's AML division.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear ultimate beneficial ownership due to non-resident shareholders and possible nominee shareholding in a Korean limited liability company.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate extract from the Korean Registry of Commerce confirming the Yuhan Hoesa registration; certified articles of incorporation; full shareholder register; beneficial ownership declaration within the bank's KYC forms; passport copies of all ultimate beneficial owners holding 25% or more; proof of source of wealth including bank statements, audited financial statements, purchase contracts, and tax records; notarized and apostilled power of attorney if a representative appears.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering red flags associated with bonded warehouse operations where customs invoices, cargo values, or logistics routing may be manipulated to transfer value across borders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid bonded warehouse license issued by Korea Customs Service; free trade zone operator approval; warehouse lease or ownership deed; customs bond certificate; recent customs entry and export declaration data; inventory ledger and reconciliation reports; purchase orders, invoices, packing lists, bills of lading, and air waybills for a 12-month historical window; annual audited financial statements; customs broker engagement agreement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk transaction pattern involving mixed currency settlements, advance payment to third parties, or rapid onshore-offshore fund movements inconsistent with the bonded warehouse commercial cycle.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Underlying purchase and sales agreements showing payment terms; LC and documentary collection drafts; SWIFT MT103 payment instructions; beneficiary KYC profiles; detailed flowcharts matching goods movement to payment flow; justification for advance or deferred payments; board minutes approving treasury policies; 12-month projected cash flow statement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, export control, and dual-use goods exposure for bonded storage in a customs free trade zone, especially if the depot may transship or re-export goods to embargoed or high-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Export control commodity classification; dual-use license or approval documents; end-user certificates; end-use statements; sanctions screening and denied party screening audit logs; country of origin certificates; bills of lading; transport insurance certificates; standard trade compliance policy manual; letter from the customs broker confirming compliance with Korea's Customs Act and Foreign Trade Act.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection from non-resident shareholders will be routed via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 through a licensed foreign exchange bank in Korea. Wire instructions must include the correct settlement currency, likely USD or KRW, and the purpose code indicating foreign direct investment or capital subscription under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. If the injection qualifies under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, the Yuhan Hoesa must file a Foreign Investment Notification before the remittance, receive a Foreign Investment Notification Certificate, and open a foreign currency deposit account in the name of the Korea-resident entity. After funds arrive, the bank issues a foreign exchange purchase confirmation, converts funds to KRW if necessary, and completes a capital verification report verifying that the paid-in capital matches the submitted financial statements and corporate registry filings. The company must retain the SWIFT receipt and bank confirmation for MOEF and customs audits.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for bonded warehouse operations will use SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for direct trade settlement, SWIFT MT700 series for confirmed or standard documentary letters of credit, and documentary collections via SWIFT MT400 series when transactions are conducted under collection terms. All payments must be cleared through a domestic Tier-1 commercial bank participating in the Korea Financial Telecommunications and Clearings Institute and the BOK-Wire large-value settlement system for KRW leg. Customs duties, bonded warehouse fees, and taxes will be paid electronically through the Korea Customs Service payment gateway using the entity's operational KRW account. For international vendor payments, the bank will require underlying contracts, invoices, customs declaration numbers, and shipping evidence to comply with trade-based AML screening.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forward contracts with licensed domestic banks, limited to underlying trade or capital exposure
KRW/USD and KRW/EUR currency swaps for cross-border trade financing and refinancing risk management
FX options and collars whose notional does not exceed verified underlying receivables or payables
FX rollover enabled by the corporate's foreign currency deposit account at a licensed Korean bank
Non-deliverable forwards restricted to qualified institutional transactions with regulatory approval and supporting documentation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Corporation Tax Base and Amount Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) - Jurisdictional District Tax Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year; for a December 31 year-end, no later than March 31 of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file incurs an additional income tax penalty of 20% of the unreported taxable amount; unpaid tax bears a daily late-payment interest charge of 0.025% under the Framework Act for National Taxes; persistent delinquency enables asset seizure and, if the entity is inactive for at least 6 months, administrative closure of the business registration, leading to eventual corporate strike-off by the court.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Local Corporate Income Tax Surcharge Return (Local Income Tax on Corporate Tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial or Metropolitan Local Government through the Local Tax Information System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same statutory filing window as the national corporate income tax return: within 3 months after fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, by March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Local income tax is a 10% surtax on corporate income tax; late filing incurs a 20% additional penalty on the local tax due plus daily overdue surcharges; chronic non-payment permits local tax seizure and revocation of the entity's free trade zone business operation approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Semi-Annual Value-Added Tax Return (covering bonded warehouse service and customs-controlled supply records)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) - Jurisdictional District Tax Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First half-year (January 1 to June 30): file by July 25 of the same year; second half-year (July 1 to December 31): file by January 25 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid VAT is subject to an additional penalty tax of 10% of the unreported amount plus a daily overdue surcharge; misstatement of customs-exempt bonded transactions may additionally attract customs surcharges up to 40% of evaded duties and an NTS administrative fine.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Bonded Warehouse and Free Trade Zone Operator Inventory and Customs Compliance Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Customs Service (KCS) and the Free Trade Zone Administrator under the Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 31 of the year following the reporting year; must include opening and closing bonded stock quantities, movement summaries, and proof of customs duty accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-submission or false inventory records breaches the Korean Customs Act and the Free Trade Zones Act; uncovered bonded stock may be immediately assessed for customs duties with a surcharge of up to 40% of evaded duty; KCS may impose administrative fines up to KRW 30,000,000, suspend or revoke the bonded warehouse license, and order removal of all bonded goods, resulting in forced closure of the depot.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Audit Report and Audited Financial Statements Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the DART electronic disclosure system and the external auditor appointed at the Annual General Meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after fiscal year-end for entities subject to mandatory external audit; if no statutory audit is required, financial statements must still be adopted and documented at the annual meeting within 3 months of year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Where mandatory, failure to appoint an auditor or file audited statements triggers sanctions under the Act on External Audit and Accounting Standards, including administrative fines up to KRW 50,000,000 per violation, orders to undergo a new audit at the company's expense, and court-ordered dissolution or strike-off for repeated refusal.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary General Meeting of Members / Yuhan Hoesa Annual Accounts Adoption
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate governance act under the Korean Commercial Act; recorded in the corporate minute book and disclosed through FSS/DART if the entity is audit-subject
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of each fiscal year; for a December 31 year-end, by March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the ordinary meeting does not automatically dissolve the Yuhan Hoesa but breaches director or manager fiduciary duties; a court may order the meeting upon member petition, and repeated failure in a free trade zone context can support revocation of the bonded warehouse license.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Yuhan Hoesa is subject to mandatory independent CPA audit under the Korean Act on External Audit and Accounting Standards if any of the following quantitative thresholds is met at the preceding fiscal year-end: total assets of KRW 5,000,000,000 or more (approximately USD 3,850,000 at 1,300 KRW/USD); total annual revenue or turnover of KRW 10,000,000,000 or more (approximately USD 7,700,000); an average workforce of 300 or more employees; or designation as a public-interest company by the Financial Services Commission. Free trade zone bonded depot operators may also be required to audit earlier by the Korea Customs Service or financial regulator based on customs duty exposure or enhanced AML and foreign exchange compliance triggers.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) applies to externally audited Yuhan Hoesa entities; otherwise, Korean GAAP and the simplified accounting standards for small and medium enterprises under the Act on External Audit and Accounting Standards and the Korean Commercial Act apply. All tax records must follow the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Corporate Income Tax Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No standalone annual beneficial ownership confirmation filing is imposed on a purely domestic Korean Yuhan Hoesa. However, if the entity is foreign-invested, any change in shareholding or beneficial ownership must be reported to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy through KOTRA or an authorized Foreign Exchange Bank within 30 days of the closing transfer under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. Domestically, the Register of Members must be updated immediately upon any transfer, and Korea Customs Service free trade zone bonded operator records require updated control-person declarations whenever a controlling owner changes. Annual re-confirmation is therefore satisfied through the corporate tax return, the annual meeting records, and the customs inventory compliance return.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Korea applies a progressive national corporate income tax (CIT) of 10% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million, 20% from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion, and 22% above KRW 20 billion; plus a local corporate income tax surcharge equal to 10% of the national CIT, producing an all-in top headline effective rate of 24.2% on the marginal taxable base above KRW 20 billion.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Eligible foreign-invested enterprises operating in Korean Free Trade Zones under the Act on Designation and Management of Free Trade Zones and the Restriction of Special Taxation Act may receive a 100% CIT exemption for the first three years and a 50% reduction for the following two years, or a five-year full exemption depending on the project category, together with local tax reductions and exemption from customs duties on inbound capital goods for bonded warehousing; additional R&D tax credits of up to 25% of qualifying R&D expenditures and vocational training/employment tax credits also reduce the effective rate, and during the statutory exemption window the effective Korean entity-level tax rate can be 0% on qualifying FTZ income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Korean Corporate Income Tax Return (Corporate Tax Base and Tax Amount Return, legally designated as the Corporate Tax Return under Article 60 of the Korean Corporate Tax Act; form codes commonly referenced as HomeTax Form 110/202/211) filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic filing portal (www.hometax.go.kr, multi-lingual electronic tax invoice and return system for non-residents).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with a mandatory interim corporate income tax prepayment (semi-annual estimated tax) for corporations whose fiscal year exceeds six months; the final annual return reconciles interim prepayments and withholding credits.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual CIT return and payment must be filed and paid within three months after the close of the fiscal year for a domestic corporation (for a calendar-year taxpayer, March 31 of the following year); a one-month extension is available upon application or when audited financial statements and tax-return preparation by a Korean certified tax attorney/licensed accountant mandate the later statutory extended date, but no separate extension for the payment obligation is granted, so interest accrues on any unpaid balance after the three-month primary deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Registered Entity and Business Identity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Domestic corporation name, business registration number, fiscal year beginning and end dates, main industrial classification code (ISIC 5210 / warehouse and transport auxiliary / bonded warehouse operation), FTZ bonded depot license number, head office address, foreign-investment registration number if applicable, and tax representative details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Yuhan Hoesa (Korean LLC) with non-resident shareholders, Box 1 must disclose the appointed Korean tax representative for foreign investors; the physical warehouse must be expressly identified as located inside a customs-bonded free trade zone; if the license name, foreign investment declaration, and corporate registration mismatch, the National Tax Service and Korea Customs Service will coordinate a joint non-resident compliance audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Gross Revenue and Interim Prepayment Reconciliation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross receipts from bonded warehouse storage fees, handling and loading fees, inventory management, freight forwarding, customs declaration service fees, and ancillary logistics revenue; separately disclosed domestic consumption revenue versus export-oriented bonded-depot revenue; interim paid-in corporate income tax for the current fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All revenue generated in connection with the Korean bonded depot must be recognized in the Korean tax return of the Yuhan Hoesa and cannot be diverted to an offshore parent merely because the customer contract is signed by a non-resident affiliate; foreign-currency USD-denominated warehouse charges must be translated into KRW at the tax statutory exchange rate, and foreign exchange gains are taxable; ensure no export-revenue misclassification where goods are actually consumed in the Korean domestic market.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income is calculated as gross income less deductible expenses, non-taxable income, loss carryforwards, and deductions under special tax incentives; the final tax base is the taxable amount subject to progressive corporate income tax rates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recharges from non-resident shareholders for head-office management, marketing, information technology, or royalty fees are deductible only if they are arm's-length, documented by written contracts, practically rendered, and supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation; expenses paid to a foreign parent without technical service substance or with excessive mark-up must be added back to the Korean taxable base, and any disallowed amount may be recharacterized as a constructive dividend or deemed royalty subject to 22% withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Computed Corporate Income Tax and Deductions/Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT is computed by applying the progressive statutory rates to the taxable base; foreign-investment FTZ exemptions, R&D credits, employment credits, emergency tax credits, and other non-refundable credits are applied to derive the net corporate income tax before prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Yuhan Hoesa claims a statutory FTZ foreign-investment CIT exemption, it must attach the official project approval issued by the Ministry of Economy and Finance / local free-trade-zone authority; only income from the approved FTZ logistics activity qualifies, and income from passive holding, management charges, or domestic trading will be disallowed; local corporate income tax surcharge recapture must be calculated when an exemption or reduction is incorrectly claimed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Prepaid Taxes, Withholding Credits, and Foreign Tax Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: This box records interim tax payments already made, domestic tax withheld at source on interest, dividend, royalty, and service income, excess foreign tax credits, and any other taxes treated as advance payments against the final CIT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For the Korean LLC, include corporate tax prepayments remitted during the year; if the entity has received dividends or interest from foreign subsidiaries, a foreign tax credit may be available only with an official foreign tax receipt and treaty filing; in the outbound structure, when the Korean entity pays dividends, interest, or royalties to a non-resident parent, the 22% withholding tax must be remitted separately through HomeTax by the 10th day of the month following payment and may not be deducted as a corporate expense.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Net Tax Payable or Refund
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final calculation of net CIT payable after all credits, interim prepayments, withholding credits, and local income tax surcharge; the amount shown is the additional tax due or the refundable excess.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any final net tax must be paid by the statutory deadline; if the return generates a refund, NTS will apply it against outstanding tax liabilities; for entities without full-time Korean staff, payment must be remitted through the electronic HomeTax trust/site account, and the director must ensure that the corporate bank account is funded to avoid late-payment interest and the automatic blocking of the foreign director's departure from Korea on tax-default blacklist grounds.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - International Transactions and Transfer Pricing Schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory declaration of all controlled transactions with foreign related parties, including cross-border purchases, sales, service fees, financing charges, royalty and licensing transactions, warehouse sublease fees, and any payments to shareholders in Free Trade Zone or customs-bonded operations; transfer pricing method selected, and Local File/Master File/CbC report availability is indicated.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Korean LLC in a FTZ, every intercompany transaction with its non-resident shareholder (storage tariff, equipment rental, software license, management fee, logistics agency, loans) must be covered by an arm's-length pricing policy using the most reliable OECD method; the Korean transfer pricing schedules must be attached even if no transfer pricing adjustment is sought, because omission is treated as non-disclosure and will trigger a 30% penalty on any later tax adjustment; Schedule 501 and supporting local-file documentation must be contemporaneous and signed by the Korean tax representative.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the Corporate Income Tax Return triggers an additional tax equal to 20% of the unpaid tax under Article 75 of the Korean Corporate Tax Act; under-reporting or overstating deductions generates a 10% additional tax on the underlying misreported amount; late payment accrues daily statutory interest at the Bank of Korea base rate plus approximately 3.5 percentage points per annum (currently about 7% per annum) from the original due date until payment; failure to prepare or submit transfer pricing documentation under the International Tax Adjustment Act triggers a 30% penalty on any transfer pricing adjustment, and the failure to file a CbC Report can trigger separate administrative fines; behavior that crosses into deliberate fraud is prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act, with fines up to five times the evaded tax and maximum imprisonment of five years on ordinary tax evasion, and aggravated imprisonment up to 12 years under the Special Act on Aggravated Punishment of Certain Economic Crimes where the tax evaded exceeds approximately KRW 500 million.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: The statutory Korean withholding tax rate for dividends remitted by a Korean domestic corporation to non-resident shareholders is 22% in aggregate, comprising 20% national withholding tax and 2% local income tax surcharge; DTA-reduced rates commonly apply at 15% for portfolio dividends and 5% for a foreign corporate shareholder holding at least 25% of the Korean company's shares, subject to documentary proof and limitation-on-benefits review.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim bilateral tax treaty (DTA) relief on outbound dividends, interest, or royalties from the Yuhan Hoesa, the non-resident beneficial owner must: (1) obtain an original Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the competent tax authority in the jurisdiction of residence, dated within the calendar year of payment or the year immediately preceding; (2) complete and file with the Korean payer on the HomeTax system the Statement of Exemption/Reduction of Non-Residents Tax Withholding, together with a beneficial ownership declaration confirming the recipient controls, has the direct right to receive, and is not contractually committed to pass the payment onward to another person; (3) where the reduced dividend rate is claimed, provide shareholding registration records evidencing continuous share ownership for at least 12 months as required by the relevant DTA; (4) substantiate economic substance by providing proof of foreign-resident offices, employees, domestic board decisions, balance-sheet evidence of investment capacity, and no contract-netting or backward-to-back arrangements; and (5) if taxes were withheld at the statutory rate and the relief application is made after payment, file a claim for refund with the competent Korean district tax office within five years, attaching the same TRC and all transaction agreements plus proof of the actual Korean tax remitted to the National Tax Service.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The statutory Korean withholding tax on cross-border royalties and interest payments to non-residents is also 22% in aggregate (20% national plus 2% local income tax); treaty-reduced rates vary by jurisdiction and generally range from 10% to 15% for interest and royalties, and certain technical-service/intangible royalties may be exempt from Korean source taxation if the non-resident provides the technology through a qualifying DTA provision and has no Korean permanent establishment; intercompany interest must be at arm's-length rates, supported by loan agreements, actual cash flows, and market benchmark analysis, and excessive interest may be recharacterized as a dividend or denied a deduction if the Korean debtor is thinly capitalized.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10,000,000,000 in annual controlled transactions with foreign related parties involving tangible goods, or KRW 5,000,000,000 involving services, intangible property, and loans, triggers mandatory Local File preparation and filing in Korea under the International Tax Adjustment Act; Master File preparation is required when aggregate controlled foreign-related-party transactions equal at least KRW 50,000,000,000; and a Country-by-Country Report is required where the Korean ultimate parent or top-tier Korean constituent entity belongs to an MNE group with consolidated revenue of KRW 100,000,000,000 or more in the preceding fiscal year.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not use the label 'Economic Substance Regulations' but enforces substance-over-form through Article 14 of the Basic Act for National Taxes, the beneficial ownership provisions of each double tax treaty, and the Korean General Anti-Abuse Rule (GAAR) to deny treaty benefits and to disregard a corporation where the Korean Yuhan Hoesa cannot demonstrate day-to-day management, local employees, physical bonded warehouse facilities, real operational risk, and meaningful income-generating activity in Korea; for a bonded depot company, Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) include physical custody of goods, Korean customs clearance management, inventory control, storage and release decisions, revenue negotiation and invoicing, and operational risk assumption - all of which must be performed by the Korean entity rather than a shell-service provider, and the economic substance test will be applied in transfer pricing audits to confirm the entity is the true beneficiary of the Korean FTZ income.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and False Corporate Income Tax Filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The directors of the Yuhan Hoesa deliberately under-declare bonded-warehouse revenue by invoicing Korean customers through an offshore affiliate, fail to record cash payments for storage and handling, transfer funds to foreign bank accounts without reflecting taxable income, or fabricate rental, construction, or logistics expense deductions in the Corporate Income Tax Return to eliminate the Korean tax base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: This violates Article 60 of the Corporate Tax Act and constitutes tax evasion under Article 11 of the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act, exposing the company to fines of up to five times the total evaded national corporate income tax and local surcharge, plus additional penalties of 20% for non-reporting and 10% for understatement; where the evaded amount exceeds approximately KRW 500 million, the Special Act on Aggravated Punishment of Certain Economic Crimes can raise the criminal imprisonment range to three to twelve years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Korean tax collection law pierces the corporate veil through the secondary tax liability doctrine of Article 39 of the National Tax Collection Act, making a responsible director or actual oligopolistic shareholder personally liable for unpaid corporate tax, penalties, and interest where the company willfully manipulated returns and its assets are insufficient; the National Tax Service will place the director on the serious tax-offender blacklist, issue an overseas travel ban, freeze personal bank accounts, and seize personal real property; a criminal conviction also carries imprisonment of up to five years for ordinary evasion or up to twelve years for aggravated evasion, in addition to disqualification from serving on boards in Korea.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and False International Transaction Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Sophisticated cross-border intercompany fee arrangements in which Yuhan Hoesa pays the foreign parent inflated service, royalty, software, management, and warehouse-lease charges, or intentionally centralizes intellectual property or procurement profit offshore so that the Korean FTZ entity is left with no margin, combined with failure to file Schedule 501 or to prepare contemporaneous Local File/Master File documentation, creates a high-risk transfer pricing audit target.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Articles 4 and 5 of the International Tax Adjustment Act, National Tax Service may re-determine the taxable income using the arm's-length principle and impose, in addition to the CIT difference, a 10% underreporting penalty and a 30% documentation penalty of the adjusted transfer-pricing amount, as well as statutory late-payment interest; knowingly preparing false transfer-pricing invoices or deliberately omitting controlled transactions with foreign related parties can be prosecuted as tax fraud under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act, attracting fines of up to five times the evaded tax and imprisonment of up to five years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who signed or instructed the false transfer-pricing documents may be jointly and severally liable with the Korean corporation for the adjusted tax, unpaid foreign withholding, and penalties under the secondary liability rules if the corporation cannot pay; Korean courts can impose personal asset recovery and require the director to repatriate shifted funds from the offshore parent, and the National Tax Service will issue an overseas departure prohibition pending payment; in egregious asset-shifting cases, directors face criminal imprisonment of up to five years for documentation fraud, with aggravated punishment when foreign banking channels were used to conceal taxable profits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Bonded Depot Customs Duty Evasion and Sham Economic Substance / Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The FTZ bonded warehouse company illegally withdraws imported or bonded goods into the Korean domestic market without paying customs duties, files false customs declarations for goods that are permanently consumed domestically, or is used as a paper-shell Korean entity with no physical staff or operational activity, created solely to access Korea's customs-free zone benefits and bilateral tax treaty network for dividends, interest, and royalties from a direct non-resident shareholder.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: This triggers criminal penalties under Articles 270 and 271 of the Korean Customs Act for smuggling and duty evasion, including imprisonment of up to ten years and fines of up to five to ten times the evaded customs duties and applicable value-added tax; for the tax treaty dimension, Korean tax authorities will deny the DTA withholding reduction entirely, retroactively assess the full 22% withholding tax on outbound dividends and royalties, and levy neglected-tax penalties; the misuse of an FTZ license is also an administrative license-revocation event under the Act on Designation and Management of Free Trade Zones, and illegal bonded transactions can lead to closure of the warehouse.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Korean Customs and tax authorities disregard the corporate form where the entity is a mere conduit or sham for tax-avoidance; directors who ordered employees to release bonded goods without duty payment or who attempted to conceal the shell nature of the Korean company will be pursued personally as principals in the smuggling offense, with travel bans, blacklisting, seizure of personal property, and imprisonment of up to ten years; a director who knowingly allowed the Korean LLC to be used for treaty shopping without genuine CIGA in Korea faces secondary liability for the entire unpaid Korean tax and civil restitution of diverted funds from the foreign parent, and the court can lift the corporate veil to attach the director's personal assets.
